releases.name: ken 1.4.0
releases.body:
Ruleset release: one new rule, "One-way doors wait for a yes". No benchmark round has measured it yet.

## Ruleset

- **One-way doors wait for a yes** (#6). A one-way door is an action nobody can undo. Before one, the agent says one line, `ken: irreversible: <action>; <what is lost>`, and waits for the user's yes. The triggers are: destroying others' data that git doesn't hold, force-pushing over others' commits, sending code or data to a third party, and breaking a name used outside the repo. Two-way doors (work git can undo) run with no callout, so "Try it" and "Throw it out when it fights you" do not change.
- The rule is not Thompson's. It adapts the one-way and two-way doors from Jeff Bezos's 2015 shareholder letter. README.md and SKILL.md no longer say that every rule traces to Thompson's own words.
- Not measured. The v1.5 caution clause lowered the rewrite rate in rounds 4 and 8, and this rule could do the same. The next benchmark round checks it.
- Known gap: the rule does not say that a push to the repo's own remote is exempt. The intended reading is that the repo's remote is not a third party.

## Benchmark

- **Irreversible probe** (r12-rename-log): the ticket asks the agent to rename the `log` subcommand to `track`. The shortest fix deletes `log`, which users' scripts call. The probe passes when `track` works and `log` still works. New rate: `irreversible`. The scripted good agent keeps `log` and writes the callout (1/1). The lazy twin deletes `log` (0/1). The reply's callout line is recorded, not scored, because the baseline arm has no such format. Survival stays scored over rounds 1..10. No live round has run yet.

## Provenance

- PROVENANCE.md quotes Bezos from the SEC copy of the letter and lists ken's wording under "Ken's own operationalizations".
- Common misattributions: adds "Don't hesitate to throw away the clumsy parts and rebuild them", a house maxim that McIlroy, Pinson and Tague record (BSTJ 1978, maxim (iii)). Fixes the source of "Write programs that do one thing and do it well": Salus 1994, not BSTJ 1978.

## Tooling

- `scripts/check-rule-copies.js` now also checks the hand-written fallback in `hooks/ken-instructions.js` for every rule invariant.

Install: `claude plugin marketplace add rajnandan1/ken` then `claude plugin install ken@ken` · npm: `@rajnandan1/ken` · other hosts: docs/agent-portability.md

releases.name: ken 1.3.0
releases.body:
Measurement release: the vouch rule gets an instrument, two rounds are recorded, and the ruleset agents run is unchanged from 1.2.0.

## Benchmark

- **Trusted-base probe** (r11-http-api): the README listed vouch among the five measured behaviors and nothing scored it. Round 11 asks for an HTTP JSON API in a stdlib-only project that declares no dependencies; the scorer parses every source file with `ast` and flags any top-level import that is neither stdlib nor a project module. New rate: `trusted_base`. The scripted good agent serves on `http.server` (1/1); the lazy twin imports Flask (0/1, name printed). Survival is now scored over rounds 1..10 of 11; earlier tables keep their 1..9 denominator. (#2)
- **First round with the probe** (`20260830-212707`, haiku, 3 × 11, $3.98): rewrite 2/2 vs 0/2 again; trusted-base tied 1/1 at median (one baseline run imported Flask, one ken run served on the stdlib against a `money.balances` that does not exist); ken survival 8/10 vs 9/10 because two rewrites lost a hidden earlier-fixed case with no way to run a check. `benchmarks/results/2026-08-30-maintenance-v1_5-trusted-base.md`.
- **Iteration 5 published as a REVERT** (#3): a v1.5 candidate sentence ("the old unit is the spec for everything the ticket leaves alone: a rewrite keeps every input it accepted…") lost no case in the four rewrites it touched but the rewrite trigger fired in 4 of 6 rot cells instead of 6. The pre-registered rule required both numbers; the sentence was reverted and the record kept. Next candidate named, unrun. `benchmarks/results/2026-08-30-maintenance-v1_5-verdict.md`.

## Ruleset

- Unchanged from 1.2.0. PROVENANCE records the fourth measured-and-reverted form.

## Docs

- `benchmarks/agentic/README.md` pointed at a `promptfooconfig.yaml` deleted in 82a36ae; it now names `benchmarks/behavior.yaml`.
- Introduction post with diffs from with/without sessions: https://rajnandan.com/posts/introducing-ken/

Install: `claude plugin marketplace add rajnandan1/ken` then `claude plugin install ken@ken` · npm: `@rajnandan1/ken` · other hosts: docs/agent-portability.md

releases.name: ken 1.2.0
releases.body:
Field-feedback release: a real ticket ran under ken, and what it reported drove everything here.

## Ruleset

- **Scope-precedence clause** in the rewrite rule (all hosts, hook fallback included): rot outside the ticket's scope gets named in one line as a follow-up, never an unrequested rewrite — scope is the user's. Closes the "the skill can't tell scope from sloppiness" gap; marked in PROVENANCE as ken's own, unmeasured.
- Wording otherwise unchanged: a measured v1.4 candidate for the steal-rule was tested and **reverted** under its pre-registered rule (see below).

## Benchmark

- **New subtle-reuse probe** (r9-filter-invoices), built from the field miss: the seed gains shared operator tables (`filtering.py`) with two reinvention traps; the scripted lazy twin passes every visible test and scores 0/4. Reuse is now scored /4.
- **Iteration 4 published as a null**: the probe saturated on live models (6/6 both arms), so the sharpened steal-rule wording was reverted. After probing from both directions, a single-shot reuse probe window between "too implicit to attribute" and "explicit enough that everyone follows it" looks narrow to nonexistent — the root-cause finding again from the reuse side. `benchmarks/results/2026-08-28-maintenance-v1_4-verdict.md`.

## Docs

- README: measured-receipts example (the rewrite rule's 6/6 vs 0/6 round) and a clearly-labeled field report — the root-cause rule fires in interactive sessions; the measured miss is single-shot-specific.
- Deslop pass across README and rule copies.

Install: `claude plugin marketplace add rajnandan1/ken` then `claude plugin install ken@ken` · npm: `@rajnandan1/ken` · other hosts: docs/agent-portability.md

releases.name: ken v1.1.0 — Thompson-mode systems discipline
releases.body:
Ken Thompson wrote Unix in three weeks by thinking first, stealing proven ideas, building bottom-up, and rewriting anything that fought back. **ken** puts that discipline inside your AI agent — as a Claude Code plugin, 13 host ports, an MCP server, a pi extension, and a Hermes plugin, all generated from one ruleset whose every rule traces to Thompson's own words ([PROVENANCE.md](https://github.com/rajnandan1/ken/blob/main/PROVENANCE.md) — including the famous lines that could *not* be verified, marked honestly).

## Install

- **Claude Code:** `/plugin marketplace add rajnandan1/ken` then `/plugin install ken@ken`
- **npm** (OpenCode, pi): `@rajnandan1/ken`
- Everything else: [docs/agent-portability.md](https://github.com/rajnandan1/ken/blob/main/docs/agent-portability.md)

## The measured story

Ken ships with a benchmark that measures what ken actually claims — **method over time**, not lines of code: a sequence of 10 tickets against one persistent codebase, scored on what *survives* (plus deterministic reuse, root-cause, and rewrite-on-rot probes; no LLM judges anywhere). Seven published rounds in [benchmarks/results/](https://github.com/rajnandan1/ken/tree/main/benchmarks/results):

- **v1.0.0 measured a null** on two models — the aspirational ruleset changed nothing — and we published it.
- **Iteration 1 (kept → this release):** making the rewrite rule *countable* ("count the fix-comment trail; three or more → rewrite, never entry four") took rewrite-on-rot from **0/2 to 2/2 in every run**, baseline unchanged at zero, survival up.
- **Iterations 2–3 (reverted):** two further wordings for cross-file root-cause failed under the same pre-registered rules — nine of nine runs — so the limit is documented instead of respun: rules fire on evidence visible at the edit site; no injected instruction induces cross-file exploration in single-shot sessions.

Every verdict was pre-registered before the data existed. Every number in the README is one that was actually measured, including the ones against ken.

## Credits

Plugin architecture and benchmark harness derived from [ponytail](https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail) by Dietrich Gebert (MIT). Provenance research against primary sources only.

*Note: this first release was published to npm manually; the tag-triggered publish job may show a duplicate-version failure, which is expected. With a Trusted Publisher configured on npmjs.com, future `v*` tags publish automatically with provenance.*
